bounds.lower_bound_method: Deleting 7 columns from any CA(4;20,2) yields a CA(4;13,2). Izquierdo-Marquez and Torres-Jimenez prove CAN(4,13,2)=32, so CAN(4,20,2)>=32.
bounds.upper_bound_source: Colbourn frozen November 2024 table, k=20, t=4, v=2.
bounds.gap: 32 <= CAN(4,20,2) <= 39. The cited paper proves the 13-column value, not the 20-column value. No exact proof for CAN(4,20,2) was located in this bounded source check.

independent_recomputation.method: Enumerate all C(20,4)=4845 four-column projections and all 16 binary patterns per projection.

search_metadata.algorithm: 256 seeded random rows, exact uncovered-pattern repair, then seeded greedy row deletion

verification.source_review: Sol independently checked the same-parameter sources and the limits listed in PLAN.md.

limitations: The Colbourn 39-row construction has no witness at the cited table URL. It is recorded as a reported upper bound, not a reproduced result.
The NIST 65-row IPOG-F witness is a reproduced human-method baseline and is weaker than the Colbourn report.
The lower bound 32 follows from the proven 13-column subproblem. The interval remains open by seven rows.
The open-status source check included the arXiv paper and frozen Colbourn tables plus exact-parameter searches. It is not a complete literature survey.
